priorStatuses.title: Handle missing cache entries before trimming

findings.title: [P1] Stop logging issued tokens verbatim
findings.body: Every issued token is passed to `audit`, which writes it to `console.log`. Where application output is retained or centrally accessible, users with log access can recover and replay active credentials.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a login request, an attacker-controlled absolute URL or unsafe scheme is passed directly to `location.assign`, enabling an open redirect. Parse the value and permit only trusted same-origin destinations.

findings.title: [P1] CAND-TOKEN-LOG-001 — Stop recording issued tokens in application logs
findings.body:
Every call with a usable token passes that credential to `audit`, which writes it to `console.log`. In environments where console output is collected or accessible, anyone with log access can replay the token until it expires.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] CAND-OPEN-REDIRECT-001 — Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin destinations
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` comes from a login request or query parameter, a value such as `https://attacker.example/phish` now navigates the authenticated user off-site. This introduces an open redirect in the login flow and may also permit dangerous URL schemes unless the destination is parsed and allowlisted.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop logging issued tokens verbatim
findings.body:
Every call with a usable authentication token sends that credential to `console.log` through `audit`. In environments where stdout is retained or centrally accessible, anyone with log access can recover and replay issued tokens.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body:
Every caller passing a bearer, session, or API token causes that credential to be written verbatim to stdout. In environments that collect application logs, anyone with log access can reuse valid tokens to impersonate users or access protected resources.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
